title: Vulnerability Response remediation tasks and ...
content:
- **Page title:** Vulnerability Response remediation tasks and remediation task rules overview
- **Release version:** Australia
- **Updated:** March 12, 2026
- **Read time:** 6 minutes to read

## Role assignment / grouping / ownership / approvals / reviewer / authorization
- No explicit **RACI**, **responsibility matrix**, **approval**, **reviewer**, or **authorization** table is provided on the page.
- No explicit named roles beyond these are provided:
  - **analysts**
  - **remediation specialists**
  - **vulnerability admin**
  - **analyst**
- **analysts and remediation specialists**
  - Configure remediation tasks (VULs) to help them organize vulnerable items (VI) and analyze them in bulk.
- **vulnerability admin and analyst**
  - Can evaluate the remediation task rules for selected vulnerable items in the **Vulnerability Manager Workspace**.
- **assignment group**
  - Remediation task rules use the assignment group set by the **Assignment Rules** on the vulnerable item when grouping the items, and assign the remediation task to match the vulnerable items.
  - A matching Open remediation task must be assigned to the **same assignment group as the VI**.
  - If no matching task exists, the rule creates the task and **assigns it to the same assignment group as the VI**.
- **Assignment Rules module**
  - Controls the assignment of these remediation tasks as part of the default task rule.

## Remediation tasks / vulnerable items / task ownership
- Remediation tasks are used to:
  - organize vulnerable items (VI)
  - analyze vulnerable items in bulk
  - monitor progress
  - drive the remediation process more efficiently
- The criteria by which remediation tasks are formed is configured so users do not have to manually assign vulnerable items into remediation tasks.
- **Automatically update related vulnerable items** check box:
  - When selected, new VIs matching the remediation task filter criteria are automatically added to the task.
  - Vulnerable items in the remediation task that no longer match the filter criteria are automatically removed from the task.
  - By default, when the remediation task leaves the **Open** state, the check box is cleared.
  - If the **Set auto refresh vulnerable items** business rule is disabled, vulnerable items continue being added regardless of state.
  - The check box can be selected again manually from the **Under Investigation** state.
  - It is not disabled when the remediation task moves into the **Awaiting Implementation** state.
  - Once in **Awaiting Implementation**, no new vulnerable items can be added to the existing task, and existing vulnerable items cannot be removed.
- For manually created remediation tasks:
  - If VIs are added using the **Condition filter** or **Filter Group**, the check box is unchecked.
  - User can choose whether to select it.
- **Refresh associated vulnerable items** related link:
  - On the Remediation Task page, clicking it adds matching vulnerable items and removes items no longer matching.
  - It updates immediately whether or not **Automatically update related vulnerable items** is selected.
- Manually created remediation tasks using **Condition** or **Filter Group** filter types are refreshed **once an hour**.

## Deferral counts / records / modules
- Track the number of times the following can be deferred:
  - vulnerable item
  - application vulnerable item
  - container vulnerable item
  - remediation task
- A scheduled job named **set deferral counts** runs **daily**.
- It posts counts for records that are deferred **more than once** in the **Deferral count** column.
- Records are displayed in the **Multiple deferrals** modules for:
  - **VR**
  - **AVR**
  - **CVR**

## Remediation task rules / grouping / evaluation / execution
- Remediation task rules:
  - define how vulnerable items are automatically grouped and assigned
  - can group by any set of values in columns accessible from the VI
  - can automate group assignment
- Default rule:
  - **Vulnerability**
  - included in the base system
  - gathers vulnerable items based on their vulnerabilities
- Example grouping values explicitly stated:
  - configuration item (CI) support group
  - vulnerability severity
  - cost center of the vulnerable CI
  - attack vector of the vulnerability
  - low severity vulnerabilities
  - low risk CIs
  - critical servers
  - vulnerabilities with exploits
  - vulnerable items that expose the company to more risk
- Conditions:
  - You can create any number of conditions.
  - Once you set a **Group by** selection, another row appears.
  - You can have up to **six Group by selections**.
- Execution mode:
  - You can control whether all matching rules are evaluated or only the first match is applied.
  - This is set on the remediation task rules page.
  - The setting is configured in the **Security Exposure Management Workspace**.
- Rapid7 InsightVM note:
  - To make **Rapid7 InsightVM asset tags** available for use in the **Condition filter** for Remediation Task Rules, you must run the **Rapid7 InsightVM Asset List integration** before the other Rapid7 InsightVM integrations.
- Rule evaluation timing:
  - When a new vulnerable item is created, imported, or reopened after being closed, the vulnerability rules are evaluated against it.
  - A VI is only evaluated once automatically unless it is reopened after being closed or the rules are reapplied manually.
- Per-new-or-reopened-VI process:
  - For each remediation task rule, the VI is compared to the remediation task rule filter.
  - For each matching rule, the rule pulls data from the Group by selections on the VI.
  - It builds a group name and field.
  - Example group name and field given:
    - **High Risk: QID-32342:Summary of QID-3242 (Name: vulnerability ID:vulnerability summary)**
- Short description limit:
  - The **short description** field is limited to **160 characters**.
  - Longer vulnerability summaries are truncated.
- Existing task handling:
  - The rule checks for a matching **Open** remediation task assigned to the same assignment group as the VI.
  - If found, the VI is added to the existing task in the **Open** state.
  - If not found, the rule creates a **High Risk: QID-32342** task, assigns it to the same assignment group as the VI, and places the VI in the remediation task.
- Multiple rules:
  - More than one remediation task rule can be defined.
  - Too many rules may have a performance impact.
- Default assignment behavior:
  - By default, remediation task rules use the assignment group set by the **Assignment Rules** on the vulnerable item when grouping the items.
  - They assign the remediation task to match the vulnerable items.
- Deleting a rule:
  - When a task rule is deleted from the form or list view, you have the option to delete all **Open** tasks created by that rule.
  - Tasks not in the **Open** state are excluded.

## Reapplying remediation task rules
- Use the **Reapply** button on the remediation task rule page to rerun the changed rule on all active Open remediation tasks created by that rule.
- It deletes and recreates remediation tasks based on the changed rule automatically.
- **vulnerability admin** and **analyst**
  - Can evaluate the remediation task rules for selected vulnerable items in the **Vulnerability Manager Workspace**.
  - This is described as more efficient than reapplying the Remediation Task Rules in the classic UI.
- No explicit SLA, ticket field list, approval chain, or RACI matrix is provided on the page.
description: Configure remediation tasks (VULs) to help analysts and remediation specialists organize vulnerable items (VI) and analyze them in bulk. The criteria by which remediation tasks are formed is configured so that you do not have to manually assign vulnerable items into remediation tasks. Using remediation tasks, you can monitor progress and drive the remediation process more efficiently.
